description:
**Divergence** — crate-level rustdoc "Design:" section naming pattern:
- jscalendar (src/lib.rs:18, 30): one section `## Design: newtype wrappers for scalar temporal values`, then one section `## Spec-driven divergences (deliberate, do not "fix")` listing three items
- jscontact (src/lib.rs:16, 60, 96, 114, 127): five separate sections each titled `## Design: X` — `## Design: optional fields and Option<...>`, `## Design: cross-field invariants are not type-enforced`, `## Design: numeric-range bounds are not type-enforced`, `## Design: @type discriminator`, `## Design: Resource-derived types`

**Caller-observable cost**: none directly.

**Maintainer cost**: a future sibling type crate copying one or the other copies a different pattern. The aggregated `## Spec-driven divergences` style is more compact but harder to grep for individual items; the per-item `## Design: X` style is more discoverable. Neither is wrong, but the canonical-template propagation rule requires one to be picked.

**Fix**: pick a workspace convention (probably the jscontact per-item style, since the workspace's `bd remember` discipline favors granular discoverable items) and propagate to jscalendar-types. Small doc rewrite; no code changes.
title: jscalendar-types AGENTS.md uses one 'Spec-driven divergences' rustdoc section; jscontact-types uses five separate 'Design: X' sections — divergent doc-organization for canonical-template propagation
